mainTopic: How 'מחרצנים ועד זג' works as a פרט for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and where רבי אלעזר learns the method of פרט וכלל ופרט.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a statement that points to the נזיר verse 'from pits to grape skin' as the model of a פרט. The גמרא asks how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה can treat that phrase as a detail, since he uses it to teach that a נזיר is liable only for two pits and a skin. The first answer is that he follows רבי אלעזר's method of מיעט וריבה. The second answer is that he follows the רבנן. The phrase's place after the כלל makes it the פרט, and its odd wording, plural pits with a singular skin, teaches his minimum amount. The גמרא then asks where רבי אלעזר himself learns the method of פרט וכלל ופרט. רבי אבהו says it comes from the verse about giving animals to a friend to guard. רבא says it comes from the verse about bringing a קרבן from the flock. רב יהודה מדיסקרתא asks רבא why he does not use an earlier verse in the same chapter, 'from the animals, from the herd and the flock.' רבא begins to explain why that verse cannot serve, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse in נזיר as the model of a detail
steps.stepSummary: An earlier statement ends by pointing to 'מחרצנים ועד זג' in the נזיר passage as an example of how the Torah lists a detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: …in the same way that the Torah spelled out for you, regarding a נזיר: 'From pits to grape skin.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a statement that began on the previous daf. It uses the נזיר verse 'from pits to grape skin' as the example of a detail (פרט). It sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement treats 'from pits to grape skin' as a פרט, a specific item listed in the verse. That reading is the basis for the coming question. If someone uses this phrase for a different law, can it still count as a פרט?

keyTerms.meaning: specified, listed a specific detail
a detail: a specific item in a verse
grape pits/seeds
grape skin
a person who took a vow of נזירות, forbidden in grape products

phrases.english: in the manner that it specified for you regarding a nazir:
"From pits to grape skin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מחרצנים ועד זג' in נזיר serves as a model פרט.

steps.title: How can רבי אלעזר בן עזריה treat the phrase as a detail?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses 'from pits to grape skin' for the rule of two pits and a skin. So where does he get the detail?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who uses this phrase 'from pits to grape skin' to teach that a נזיר is not liable unless he eats two pits and a skin, where does he get the detail from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier reading from the viewpoint of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. He has already 'used up' the phrase for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads the phrase as setting a minimum amount: two pits and one skin. If the phrase is busy teaching that, it seems it cannot also serve as the פרט. So how would he get the detail needed for this method of interpretation?

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who says a נזיר is liable only for two pits and a skin
establishes, sets up (a verse for a certain purpose)
liable (for punishment)
from where does he derive it?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
who sets up this phrase, "from pits to grape skin,"
to say that he is not liable
unless he eats two pits and a skin,
from where does he get the detail?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה דְּקָא מוֹקֵים לְהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the use of the phrase as a פרט according to one תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'מחרצנים ועד זג' as a פרט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses the phrase for a minimum-amount rule, so it seems unavailable to serve as a detail.

steps.title: He follows רבי אלעזר's method of restricting and amplifying
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads this verse with the method of מיעט וריבה, not כלל ופרט. So he does not need the phrase as a detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי אלעזר, who interprets this verse with the method of 'restricted and amplified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses a different interpretation method. That method does not require a פרט here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two styles of reading such verses: כלל ופרט (general and detail) and מיעט וריבה (restricting and amplifying). If רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follows רבי אלעזר's מיעט וריבה approach, the question 'where is your detail?' falls away. He is free to use the phrase for his two-pits-and-a-skin rule.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who reads this verse with מיעט וריבה
restricted and amplified: a method that includes more than כלל ופרט does
expounds, interprets

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי אלעזר with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. They are two different תנאים, and here one is said to follow the other's method.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Elazar,
who expounds "restricted and amplified."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the תנא to a different method of interpretation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses כלל ופרט and so needs a פרט.
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses מיעט וריבה, so no פרט is needed.

steps.title: Or: he follows the רבנן, because the phrase comes after the generalization
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does use כלל ופרט. The Torah placed the phrase after the כלל, which shows it also works as a פרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say he holds like the רבנן. For if you thought the phrase only teaches what רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said, the Torah should have written 'from pits to grape skin' together with the other details. Why did it write it after the generalization? Learn from this that it is meant to be read as a generalization and a detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer. Even holding like the רבנן's כלל ופרט method, the phrase can serve as a פרט, because of where the Torah placed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the passage the Torah lists details such as wine and vinegar. Then comes the כלל, 'anything made from the grapevine.' If the phrase only taught the two-pits rule, it could have been written among those earlier details. Placing it right after the כלל signals that it is the פרט of a כלל ופרט.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer
the Sages (the majority view)
the Merciful One (the Torah)
a generalization in a verse
a generalization followed by a detail; the law is limited to the detail

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: like the Rabbis.
For if it would enter your mind
that it is as Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said,
let the Merciful One write this phrase, "from pits to grape skin,"
alongside the details.
For what law did He write it after the generalization?
Learn from this: to judge it as a generalization and a detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from where the phrase is placed in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase only teaches the two-pits-and-a-skin rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its placement after the כלל shows it also functions as the פרט.

steps.title: Maybe the whole phrase is only for כלל ופרט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the phrase comes entirely for כלל ופרט, leaving nothing for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the whole phrase comes only for this purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. If the phrase serves as a פרט, maybe that is its only job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 proved that the phrase serves as a פרט. But that seems to take away רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source for the two-pits-and-a-skin rule. Why assume the phrase teaches both?

keyTerms.meaning: but say: introduces a counter-suggestion
all of it, the whole thing

phrases.english: But say the whole phrase comes for this purpose!
phrases.notes: "This purpose" means being the detail in a generalization and a detail.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the phrase can serve both as a פרט and as the source for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the phrase is needed as a פרט, perhaps that uses it up completely.

steps.title: The odd wording teaches the second law
steps.stepSummary: If the phrase were only a פרט, the Torah could have used simpler wording. Mixing plural pits with a singular skin teaches the two-pits-and-a-skin rule, so the phrase does double duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it write either 'two pits,' or 'two skins,' or 'a pit and a skin.' Why did the Torah write 'from pits to grape skin'? Learn from it both: read it as a generalization and detail, and also read it to mean a נזיר is liable only once he eats two pits and a skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the exact wording of the phrase is unusual. That oddness is the extra hint for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simple detail could have been written with matching forms, such as both plural or both singular. Instead the Torah wrote 'pits' in the plural and 'skin' in the singular, which hints at the amount: two pits and one skin. So placement teaches כלל ופרט, and wording teaches the minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
for what law? Asks why the Torah wrote something this way
to expound, interpret
and there is also

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן's method, 'מחרצנים ועד זג' teaches two things. Its placement after the כלל makes it the פרט, and its plural/singular wording teaches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's minimum of two pits and a skin.

phrases.english: If so, let it write either "two pits,"

phrases.english: For what law did the Merciful One write "from pits to grape skin"?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לְמִידְרַשׁ בֵּיהּ כְּלָל וּפְרָט,
phrases.english: Learn from it to expound it as a generalization and a detail,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Double derivation: placement teaches one law, unusual wording teaches another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase serves only as a פרט.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual plural/singular wording adds a second teaching: two pits and a skin.

steps.title: Where does רבי אלעזר learn פרט וכלל ופרט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי אלעזר, who reads this verse with מיעט וריבה. It asks where he gets the method of פרט וכלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר, who interprets with 'restricted and amplified,' from where does he get the method of a detail, a generalization, and a detail?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about רבי אלעזר. It is setting up the next discussion, and the answer comes in the following lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אלעזר reads the נזיר verse with מיעט וריבה, the נזיר verse cannot be his source for פרט וכלל ופרט. So the גמרא asks where he learns that method from.

keyTerms.meaning: a detail, a generalization, and a detail: a method of reading verses

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar, who expounds "restricted and amplified,"
from where does he derive a detail, a generalization, and a detail?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה to רבי אלעזר himself, whose method was cited in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the method of פרט וכלל ופרט according to רבי אלעזר, who reads the נזיר verse with מיעט וריבה.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the source is the verse about guarding animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that רבי אלעזר learns פרט וכלל ופרט from the verse about giving animals to a friend to guard. The verse goes detail, then general, then detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: He learns it from this verse: "If a man gives his friend a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep" is a detail. "Or any animal" is a general statement. "To guard" goes back to a detail. When you have detail, general, detail, you only include things similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from Step 7. רבי אבהו shows a verse that has the pattern detail, general, detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse first lists specific animals (detail), then says "any animal" (general), then adds "to guard" (detail again). That is the shape of פרט וכלל ופרט. The rule for this shape: the law covers only things similar to the details, meaning things that can be guarded like these.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, he learns it (from a verse)
A detail, then a general statement, then a detail again: one method for reading a verse
Similar to the detail: only items like the listed details are included
To guard

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
He derives it from this verse:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר, and "it" is the פרט וכלל ופרט method that Step 7 asked about.

phrases.english: "And if a man gives to his fellow

phrases.aramaic: חֲמוֹר אוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ שֶׂה״ — פָּרַט,
phrases.english: a donkey, or an ox, or a sheep": that is a detail;
"or any animal": that is a general statement;
"to guard": it went back and gave a detail.
A detail, a general statement, and a detail:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may only include what is similar to the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by offering a source verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר learns פרט וכלל ופרט from the verse about a שומר: "donkey, ox, sheep" / "any animal" / "to guard".

steps.title: רבא: the source is the verse about sacrifices from the flock
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source: the verse about bringing a קרבן from the flock. "From" is a detail, "the flock" is general, and "sheep and goats" is a detail again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He learns it from this verse: "And if from" is a detail. "The flock" is a general statement. "Sheep and goats" goes back to a detail. When you have detail, general, detail, you only include things similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different answer to the same question. He finds the pattern in a verse about sacrifices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "from" means only part of something, so it limits (detail). "The flock" is broad (general). "Sheep and goats" names specific kinds (detail again). So this verse also has the shape of פרט וכלל ופרט.

keyTerms.meaning: From: a word that means only part, so it acts as a limit
The flock
Sheep and goats

steps.confusionAlert: Even a tiny word like "מִן" ("from") can count as a פרט here, because it means "only some of" and so it narrows things.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He derives it from this verse:
"And if from": that is a detail.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:10. "From" means only some, so it narrows things.

phrases.english: "The flock": that is a general statement;
"sheep and goats": it went back and gave a detail.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may only include what is similar to the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רבי אבהו to the same question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר learns פרט וכלל ופרט from "ואם מן" / "הצאן" / "כבשים ועזים".

steps.title: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא: why not use the earlier verse in the same chapter?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא challenges רבא: an earlier verse, "from the animals, from the herd and the flock," has the same pattern. Why not learn it from there?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא said to רבא: Let him learn it from this verse instead: "From" is a detail. "The animals" is a general statement. "Herd and flock" goes back to a detail. Detail, general, detail: you only include things similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא pushes back on רבא's choice of verse. He points to an earlier verse that seems to fit the same pattern just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier verse also starts with "from" (detail), then says "the animals" (general), then names "herd and flock" (detail). If it fits perfectly, why did רבא skip it and use the later verse? רבא begins to answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him learn (it from here instead)
The animals
Herd (cattle) and flock (sheep and goats)
From Diskarta, the name of a place

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Diskarta said to Rava:
But let him learn it from this verse:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:2, which comes earlier in the same chapter as רבא's verse.

phrases.english: "From": that is a detail;
"the animals": that is a general statement;

phrases.english: you may only include what is similar to the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מִדִּיסְקַרְתָּא לְרָבָא, וְלֵילַף מִן הָדֵין קְרָא

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice of ויקרא 1:10 as the source for פרט וכלל ופרט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier verse (ויקרא 1:2) has the same detail-general-detail shape, so why not learn the method from there?

steps.title: רבא explains why the earlier verse cannot be the source
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב יהודה מדיסקרתא: the earlier verse 'מן הבהמה' cannot teach פרט וכלל ופרט, because if we learned it from there, we would make a mistake about the word 'הבהמה.' The sentence stops here and finishes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You cannot learn it from this verse. If we learned it from there, I would have said that the word 'the animals'...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to answer the challenge from רב יהודה מדיסקרתא. He says the earlier verse cannot be the source, and he begins to explain why. The explanation finishes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that both verses look the same: detail, general, detail. רבא says the earlier verse has a problem. Its general word, 'הבהמה', could be read in a way that ruins the lesson. He has not yet said what that wrong reading is.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot learn it from here
From there (from that verse)
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
The animals; the general word in the earlier verse

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished. Do not think רבא's answer ends here. 'הבהמה' is the start of the wrong reading he wants to warn against, and the next line tells us what it is.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering רב יהודה מדיסקרתא's challenge from the last step.

phrases.english: From this one, you cannot learn it,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the earlier verse, 'from the animals, from the herd and the flock' (ויקרא 1:2).

phrases.english: because if it were from there, I would have said:
"The animals"…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by defending רבא's choice of verse from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two verses are not the same. The earlier verse has a word that could lead to a wrong reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses look like detail-general-detail, so either one should work as the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier verse cannot serve, because 'הבהמה' would be misread. The details follow in the next line.
